label: text
text: That anti-British agitation, following the end of the blockade of Hong Kong, will cease at Canton in four months, is the prediction made confidently by a Chinese migrant who has come here on business.

label: text
text: " Further "improvement in the situation has been recorded and attempted "examination" activities were restrained in Canton on Wednesday.

label: text

label: text

label: text
text: The Chinese people must move about in their own methods. Accordingly time was needed to restore normal conditions. The speaker gave it as a fact, and not as a surmise that definite plan had been laid down to disband the pickets and strikers.

Corley, daughter of Mr. and Mrs. A. F. Corley of Kingston on Thames, who arrived in the Colony by the s.s. "Mantua."

label: paragraph_title
text: POLICY TOWARDS CHINA.

label: paragraph_title
text: Our New Minister "Hits From the Shoulder,"

label: text
text: London, Oct. 14.

label: text
text: Lord Southborough, who presided at a China Association banquet, bade godspeed to Mr. Miles Lampson who is going to China within a week as the New Minister.

label: text
text: Mr. Lampson, responding, voiced the Government's deep sympathy with the difficulties of the Chinese people while observing strict impartiality towards the contending factions; but pending the establishment of a national government, the British Government was bound to accord their nationals the fullest protection and exact reparation for any wrong done where no Chinese authority exists.

label: text
text: Mr. Lampson paid a tribute to the patience and sacrifices of British communities in China in endeavours to overcome the difficulties which they had faced, which make it more incumbent on the Government to defend their lawful rights. Nevertheless he was confident the Chinese people would not misinterpret the attitude as implying unfriendliness to them or a desire to interfere with internal politics in China.—Reuter.

label: text
text: In order to avoid international complications (says the "Canton Gazette"), General Chang Kaishek has issued a strict order prohibiting his troops from firing upon foreign gunboats and other vessels on the Yangtse unless the latter willfully disregarded the shipping regulations instituted by the Nationalist general headquarters.

label: text
text: It will be recalled that the British Consult-General in Canton was instructed by the Minister in Peking to send a note to Mr. Eugene Chen on the matter.

label: text
text:
The note stated that British vessels have always maintained strict neutrality and have been forbidden from transporting arms.
Mr. Eugene Chen (Canton's Foreign Minister) explained to the Consul that the southern troops "known to be well disciplined, could not have taken such actions against British vessels and that the incidents might have been caused by the troops newly incorporated into the Nationalist Army.

label: text
text:
NO CHANGE ON KIANGSI
FRONT.

label: text
text: OPERATIONS ELSEWHERE.

label: text
text:
[By Our Special Correspondent.]
No material change has occurred in the Kiangzi war zone, nor does any seem imminent from the trend of hostilities.

label: text
text: Reports to hand, however, point to there being little possibility of an armistice supervening. On the contrary, it is predicted by military observers that General Chang Kai-shek is just waiting to take stock of his position before launching another drive.

label: text
text: Meanwhile the southerners are retiring gradually and slowly, with the northern Allies reluctant to keep close contact that necessitates entering the hilly country away from the Kiukiang-Nanchang Railway.

text: The position near Swatow is obscure and it is almost impossible to say which side is winning, as the engagements hitherto have been relatively unimportant.

Most of the guns and ammunition he said were being sent to the Cannonese army but large quantities were available for the defeated Kalgan troops if they should ever be reorganised.

label: text

Anxiety About Coasting
Steamer.

label: text
text: S.S. "BORNEO" OVERDUE HERE.

label: text
text: May Have Met the Typhoon Near Hainan.

label: text
text:
The Yick Tai S.S. Co., Ltd. of Hong Kong owners of the "s.s. "Borneo" (of which Capt. J. H. Van den Berg is the "skipper), are anxious as to the safety and whereabouts of their steamer, which is on the Hongau-Hong Kong run.
The local office was advised that the "Borneo" sailed from Hong Kong on Oct. 10 at daylight with a full cargo of coal consigned to the Taikoo Sugar Refining Co. here.
The "Borneo" therefore, is considerably overdue. Another point which makes those concerned uneasy is the Observatory's report of the existence of a severe typhoon near Hainan, last Sunday.
Masters of vessels sailing to Hai-phong are asked to keep a "lookout" for any sign of this steamer.
The "Borneo" is a "coasting steamer calling regularly at Hong Kong and flies the British flag.

label: paragraph_title
text: STOLEN GOODS.

label: paragraph_title
text:
WEST POINT BURGLARY
SOLVED.
PAWNSHOP ARREST

label: text
text: A watch kept by detectives at the pawnshops resulted in a clue which led to the arrest of a burglar who took two new raincoats and other clothing from No. 5, Sai On Lane (western district) on Tuesday night. All the property was recovered.

label: text
text: Entrance to the house, occupied by a rattan maker, was gained by cutting through the door with a sharp instrument and unfastening the bolt.

label: text
text: As is the usual way with thieves, the real culprit kept in the background while he hired another man to go to a pawnshop far away from the scene of the robbery to pledge part of the stolen property.

label: text
text: A detective questioned the man regarding the property and after a fruitless attempt to prove that the clothing was given to him by his sister he took the officer to Causeway Bay where he thief was waiting with the remainder of the haul.

label: text
text: When brought before Major C. Willson at the Central Magistracy this morning, the first defendant denied knowledge of the burglary, but claimed that the property was handed to him by the second defendant to pawn. This was admitted by the latter, who confessed to being the thief.

label: text
text: Divisional Inspector Grant proved a previous conviction against the second defendant. His Worship imposed sentence of four months' hard labour on the charge of larceny. The first defendant was found guilty of receiving the stolen property and was sentenced to three months' hard labour.
